newsitem.title: UK: AMB-Channel 5 retuning upsets UK retailers.
newsitem.headline: AMB-Channel 5 retuning upsets UK retailers.

text.p: The British Retail Consortium (BRC) voiced concern on Friday about the video retuning programme of the soon-to-be launched Channel 5.
The BRC, which represents some 90 percent of Britain's high street stores, fears that the plan may jeopardise the relationship between retailers and their customers.

"The prospect of other people's engineers, with perhaps varying knowledge of the specific products, not only causes worry, but may invalidate guarantees and extended warranties," the BRC said. "BRC is concerned that the problems that are likely to arise will be both costly and unpredictable."
Channel 5, which is due to begin broadcasting on January 1, 1997, must retune some 10 million video recorders nationwide to avoid interference from its signal.
It has just begun the process of sending its engineers out to households to carry out the work, which Channel 5 sees costing around 100 million stg.
The BRC said that several thousand unskilled people were being recruited to carry out the retuning and given only two days' training.

"Imagine if each new recruit makes only one mistake a week, that would result in an additional 7,000 engineering service calls per week. How is this going to be handled and by whom?" asked Hugh Clark, BRC trading policy director.
Some critics of the scheme have also dubbed it a "thieves charter".
Channel 5 Broadcasting is a consortium grouping British media companies United News & Media and Pearson Plc plus broadcaster CLT of Luxembourg and U.S. investment firm Warburg Pincus.
